params.body:
`PUT api/vehicles/{id}/update` refuses every caller whose role is not a premium trader — which is nearly all of them — and threw away what it refused. Measured over the five days `api_log` keeps: **105 attempts from sixteen different garages**, every one discarded, each carrying a complete vehicle record.

So the change is kept and the dealer decides.

## What is kept

**The difference, not the payload.** A proposal read a week later has to say what it was answering, so the old value travels beside the new one: `{"mileage": {"from": 45000, "to": 52000}}`.

**Never a price.** The list comes from `PriceHistory::FIELDS`, so there is one answer in the codebase to "which column is a price" instead of two lists that drift. A price is the dealer's own margin and the one column where a wrong value costs money.

**One open proposal per car**, recomputed on arrival. A partner resending the same record hourly would otherwise build an inbox nobody opens; what a dealer wants is the current difference, not its history. That is enforced by the database rather than hoped for in code: `open_key` carries the vehicle while the proposal is open and NULL once decided, and MySQL allows many NULLs beside one value in a unique index.

A payload that changes nothing leaves nothing behind **and clears a proposal the world has since answered**, so a dealer who applied a change by hand stops being offered it.

## For StockCars only

Behind the flag `partner_proposals`, stage `dealers`, dealer 4 — the same shape `two_factor` already uses. Sixteen garages lose changes daily and the temptation is to switch it on for all of them, but a screen nobody has validated shown to sixteen garages is sixteen conversations instead of one. The rest follow from Beheer > Functies once the proposal reads well.

## The answer to the partner does not change

Still `200` with `update-method temporary unavailable`, byte for byte. A partner relying on that shape today should not break because we started keeping something on our side.

Worth noting separately: that 200 is a lie of its own — Hexon is told the call succeeded, which is very likely why it keeps resending, roughly 21 times a day forever. Not changed here, deliberately, but it should be.

## An injectable service, not another static

`app/Support` holds 75 classes and 62 of them are pure statics, so a static would have matched its neighbours. This one is different in kind: it carries policy (which fields are protected, what counts as a change) and a lifecycle (open → applied or ignored), and it will gain an apply flow and a screen. Policy with several callers should be substitutable, so whoever uses it declares it in a constructor.

No interface and no container binding yet: there is one implementation, and one implementation behind an interface is ceremony — especially in a codebase already carrying 72 of them under an `I` prefix that is on its way out.

## Verified

Eight tests: the difference is kept with the value it replaces, a price is never proposed, a payload that changes nothing clears the proposal, the same value in another shape is not a change, a car has at most one open proposal, a decided proposal frees the car for the next one, a page of cars asks once, and the flag is in the catalogue in four languages and starts at one garage.

New rule R P3-1.11. `phpstan` green, `pint` green on the added files. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment.

## Not in here

The dealer cannot see the proposals yet. That screen is next, and it is deliberately designed against real data rather than imagined data — which is why this lands first and starts collecting.
params.title: Keep what a partner wanted to change, as a proposal for the dealer
